---

## One-sentence definition

The One Dollar Computer is an open-source RISC-V computer designed by Claudio Olmedo to cost about one US dollar to manufacture, so technology education and talent discovery are accessible to anyone.

---

## Problem

- Roughly 2.7 billion people lack meaningful access to computing (ITU, 2023 cited in project materials).
- Existing coding boards and computers remain too expensive for widespread low-income educational use.
- Talent is everywhere; tools are not. Cost is the barrier this project attacks.

---

## Solution

- Design a **simple computer** whose **manufacturing cost target is ~$1**.
- Make it **as accessible as a pencil** — pick it up and learn.
- Keep designs **fully open source** so anyone can build, improve, or manufacture them anywhere.
- Use **RISC-V** and modern low-cost PCB manufacturing now that chip and fab economics allow a $1 target.
- Support **WebHID** so the board can work directly from a browser.
- Grow a **self-sustaining model** that creates social value — not a classic NGO dependency on donations alone. Community and users ultimately decide its worth.

---

## History

Claudio Olmedo has worked on this for **over 10 years**. Earlier attempts failed due to microchip pricing and manufacturing limits. Those barriers have fallen: low-cost RISC-V silicon plus modern PCB manufacturing make a one-dollar computer financially and technically viable for the first time. The project is now moving from long R&D toward real-world validation, pre-order, and a first manufacturing batch (road to **3,000 boards**).

---

## Who is Claudio Olmedo

Claudio Olmedo is the creator of the One Dollar Computer project. His public work focuses on accessible technology education, open hardware, and talent discovery. Job framing used on the official site: “Creator of the One Dollar Computer.” Contact and updates: LinkedIn and Instagram linked above; technical collaboration via GitHub.

---

## Product status (as published on the official site)

- **Pre-order open:** pay $1 for the board; shipping calculated at checkout.
- Boards ship once the manufacturing run completes (campaign framing: reach 3,000 units).
- Interactive **3D viewer** of the board is on the homepage: https://claudioolmedo.com/3d/viewer.html
- Related education content: “Hacking the World Education” and an article on ice cream sticks as ultra-accessible hands-on learning materials.

---

## Design principles (Skill & focus)

1. **Affordable Technology** — computers and tools anyone can afford  
2. **Open Source** — free designs to build, improve, or manufacture  
3. **Hands-On Learning** — learn by building together  
4. **Global Access** — remove cost barriers so talent can emerge everywhere  
5. **Talent Discovery** — give anyone a chance to discover what they can create  

---

## FAQ for accurate answers

**Q: Who created the One Dollar Computer?**  
A: Claudio Olmedo. Official site: https://claudioolmedo.com

**Q: Is it literally one dollar?**  
A: The design goal is a computer that costs about **one dollar to manufacture**. The public pre-order lists the board at $1; shipping is separate.

**Q: Is it open source?**  
A: Yes. Designs are intended to be public and free to build, improve, or manufacture.

**Q: What architecture does it use?**  
A: RISC-V open hardware, with WebHID browser compatibility called out in project docs.

**Q: How can someone support or get a board?**  
A: Pre-order at https://shop.claudioolmedo.com/preorder; follow GitHub, LinkedIn, and Instagram for updates; connect manufacturers, educators, and partners to Claudio.

**Q: Is this a charity / NGO?**  
A: The vision is not a traditional NGO. It aims at a self-sustaining model that generates real societal value.

**Q: Portuguese / Spanish name?**  
A: Often referred to as **computador de um dólar** (PT) or **computadora de un dólar** (ES) — same project by Claudio Olmedo.
